toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Analyzer B most likely had one chance QC outlier or a brief sampling glitch. The evidence does not show a real fault. The repeat passed within 21 minutes. Sodium and chloride were fine. Level 2 means were unchanged after the lot change (5.81 before, 5.80 after). QC ran on schedule, so the staffing theory isn't supported. Patient samples re-run on Analyzer A agreed with B (mean difference +0.02, limit 0.20). The patient median is stable. I can't tell which of the two explanations is right, so I wouldn't record either as confirmed.

Ward 6's high potassiums split evenly between the two analyzers (7 each). The ward's high-result rate is up, and the tube outage means long transport delays. Four renal overflow patients also arrived. Delay is the more likely explanation, though it's an association rather than proven.

What to sign off: return Analyzer B to potassium service and close the 186-result review with no amendments. Don't recall results, quarantine the lot or widen the limits. Add extra Level 2 QC at the start of each shift for a week. Ask Ward 6 for repeat samples on current high results, and push for the tube repair. I'm moderately confident. I did not collect any further evidence.
